carries.from: F8.1 (#1645, fixes #1674): the pull request that adds check_initial_setup_menu and check_simulate_plan_fields to tests/doc_claims.py
carries.control: Established by measurement with its null control. check_simulate_plan_fields's own null control (tests/doc_claims.py:597-611) re-runs the field-extraction regex on a text copy with one documented field's backtick literal deleted, and asserts the deletion is caught -- but it assumes the anchor regex (`r"\*\*`simulate_plan`\*\*.*?Fields,\s*\n?all optional:\s*(.*?)\.\s*An empty"`) still matches the mutated text. Perturbing the anchor itself (renaming its lead-in phrase from "Fields," to "Fields:" in a copy of docs/configuration.md, leaving the schema and every documented field untouched) makes `re.search` return None; `_mutated_span.group(1)` at tests/doc_claims.py:604 then raises `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'group'` instead of a clean `R.check(..., False, ...)` FAIL -- confirmed by running the same regex pair against the perturbed text outside the harness. check_initial_setup_menu has the same shape one line earlier: `section = text.split("## Initial setup", 1)[1]...` (tests/doc_claims.py:479) raises `IndexError: list index out of range` if that heading is ever renamed, before its first `R.check` anchor runs -- confirmed the same way, renaming the heading to "## Initial configuration" in a text copy. The null control for each check demonstrates it fires on the CONTENT mutation it was written for (a dropped field, the pre-v6.6.5 wizard shape); neither demonstrates what happens when the anchor the extraction depends on stops matching, which is the actual perturbation a doc rewrite is most likely to make.
carries.remeasure: Do not trust this paragraph's line numbers: they are measured at this PR's head (docs/configuration.md, tests/doc_claims.py) and a later stage is judged against its own merge base. Re-open tests/doc_claims.py's check_initial_setup_menu and check_simulate_plan_fields, re-locate the anchor regex/split call each depends on, and re-run the same two perturbations (rename the "## Initial setup" heading; rename "Fields," to "Fields:" in the simulate_plan sentence) against a copy of docs/configuration.md at your merge base to confirm each still raises rather than reporting a clean FAIL. If either barrier already wraps its anchor lookups (an `if m is None: R.check(anchor, False, ...); return` guard, or the equivalent), the finding is void there and only applies to the arm that still crashes.
carries.brief: Before folding tests/doc_claims.py's check_initial_setup_menu (tests/doc_claims.py:468) and check_simulate_plan_fields (tests/doc_claims.py:557) into the I5 barrier -- or writing new barrier arms in the same style -- guard every anchor lookup (a `re.search` result used before a None check, a `str.split(...)[1]` on a heading that might move) so a doc rewrite that breaks the anchor produces a named `R.check` FAIL ("the anchor this check depends on no longer matches") rather than an uncaught exception that aborts the whole doc_claims.py run and hides every other arm's result behind a traceback. Demonstrate the guard by reproducing both crashes above against the unguarded code first, then showing the guarded version reports a clean FAIL under the same perturbation.

carries.from: R9-F8.3 (handoff/r9-f8-docs-3): the doc-claims lane's PR, which lands five more code-fact arms in tests/doc_claims.py before the barrier does -- check_quick_setup_promises (thermal_model facts from config_flow.py), check_card_version_tracks_stamp (VERSION + tools/release/stamp.py's rewrite_card_version against the bundled card JS), check_curve_bias_no_weekly_bound (learner observation facts), check_readme_currency_claim (resolve_currency facts), and check_service_fields (the live services registry vs the Services paragraphs, the I5 leaf this barrier was written for)
carries.control: Established by measurement with null controls at this PR's head (doc_claims: ALL 84 checks PASSED; base: 4 of 84 red on exactly the owned seams). Each arm opens with a named anchor check before any extraction: check_quick_setup_promises guards the section regex (`section_m.group(1) if section_m else ""` then an explicit anchor check), check_card_version_tracks_stamp guards both the card regex and the doc's example-version regex, check_service_fields guards the registry-vs-paragraphs intersection, and _service_field_problems reads paragraphs by .get with a skip -- so the anchor-crash shape F8.1's two arms carry (this file's first entry) is already absent from these five, demonstrated by the arms' own controls: deleting a listed field from the assign_entity paragraph re-fires the comparison, and re-inserting the pre-fix card sentences re-fires the claim scan (+2 matches).
carries.remeasure: Do not trust this paragraph's counts: they are measured at this PR's merge base (8ff6827a) and F10.4 is judged against its own. Re-run PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 tests/doc_claims.py at your merge base and confirm ALL 84 PASS, then re-run the two perturbations in this file's first entry against check_initial_setup_menu and check_simulate_plan_fields -- those two arms are F8.1's and still carry the unguarded shape; these five do not. If the cherry-pick of F8.1's arms conflicts in tests/doc_claims.py (five new sections plus runner entries landed there first), resolve by keeping both sets of sections and unioning the runner list, never by re-recording one side.
carries.brief: When folding F8.1's two arms into the barrier, fold these five in with them (or record per-arm that each already satisfies the guard rule): the barrier's own brief text -- every anchor lookup guarded so a doc rewrite yields a named R.check FAIL, never an uncaught exception -- is already met here, and the cherry-pick must not regress it. The service-fields arm's schema source (registered_service_fields unwraps voluptuous wrappers at import time) is the part most likely to move under a services.yaml or config restructure; its anchor check names that failure, keep it named.
